summative_rubric.title: K Little Programmers — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: Used during and after Lesson 5 to score against all 3 expectations.

rows.expectation_text: use directional and positional language to create and follow instructions involving movement

levels.descriptor: Cannot name directions. Mixes left and right.
Uses 1-2 direction or position words with prompts.
Independently uses 4 direction and 4 position words to create and follow instructions.
Combines direction and position words in multistep instructions.
Does not test code. Says 'no bug' without checking.
Independently tests instructions and finds and fixes bugs.
Articulates the bug location and proposes multiple fixes.

rows.expectation_text: communicate and record step-by-step instructions using symbols, words, or pictures

levels.descriptor: Independently records a 4-step code in left-to-right order.
Designs original codes for a partner to follow.

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Score during Lesson 5 capstone. Level 3 = Kindergarten-grade-level.

summative_task_script.title: Big Programmer Capstone — Summative Administration Guide
summative_task_script.purpose: Ties Lesson 5 capstone, the 4 stations, and the rubric together.
administration_steps: Before: photocopy templates, print rubric, ready Junior Programmer certificates.
Stations 1-4 (5 min each): MOVE, POSITION, RECORD, TEST.
Station 1 MOVE: 4 directions on the mat. Evidence B11.1.
Station 2 POSITION: describe Bot's spot. Evidence B11.1.
Station 3 RECORD: write a 4-step code. Evidence B11.3.
Station 4 TEST: fix a buggy code. Evidence B11.2.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Use the Capstone Template as primary evidence. Level 3 = Kindergarten-grade-level.
